correctness.rationale: Replayed RESULT.md:30–67 for the unnormalized Laplacian. A²=(k−μ)I−μA+μJ gives the r,s levels on the orthogonal complement of constants; connectedness gives r<k, and s<0<r. Interpolate e^(−tL²)=αI+βA+γJ. The α coefficient is a convex combination of two positive exponentials and β>0 for t>0; β+γ=[1−α+(v−k)β]/v>0, and diagonal entries are positive by positive definiteness. The nonedge coefficient is (1−h)/v. Each row sums to one, so its absolute sum adds twice the negative mass, exactly the claimed expression; choosing signs of any row attains it, including at t=0 and the threshold. With x=k−r and y=k−s, h′ is a positive factor times (y/x)e^{−(y²−x²)t}−1, proving the unique peak at the displayed time. Since h starts at one and tends to zero, there is exactly one subsequent crossing of one. The nonedge derivative of the kernel is −μ at zero, so h′(0)=vμ and the norm slope is 2(v−k−1)μ=2k(k−1). The inspected supplied script tests three graphs, with exact adjacency checks and floating-point time samples; no execution of that script or formal verification is claimed.
